podcast.title: Discomfort with Legal Process
podcast.body: Richard Ashcroft, along with Mick Jagger and Keith Richards, publicly expressed their discomfort and lack of intention to be involved in the complex and controversial legal processes surrounding "Bitter Sweet Symphony," indicating a desire to distance themselves from the disputes. "Tato Mink Jaer como Chris Riches en el pasado han hecho varias declaraciones respecto a todo este proceso legal tan complejo del que se han visto en versos y ellos no tenían ninguna intención de ver si en estos rollos si no lo consideran correcto."

podcast.title: Friends and Collaborator with The Chemical Brothers
podcast.body: Richard Ashcroft became an early friend and collaborator of The Chemical Brothers, contributing to their albums and solidifying their deep connections within the British rock and indie culture. "hicieron amigos de Richard Ascrow... los chemical brothers en sus iscos tienen colaboraciones con Richard Alskroff."

srcs.episode: The Chemical Brothers. Padres de la cultura BIG BEAT

podcast.title: Grammy Nomination as Composer
podcast.body: Despite the intricate legal situation that saw Allen Klein acquire 100% of "Bitter Sweet Symphony"'s rights, Richard Ashcroft, alongside Mick Jagger and Keith Richards, was nominated for a Grammy for "Best Song of the Year" as a composer of the track. This situation, where he was nominated for a song he didn't entirely compose and no longer owned, is a notable curiosity. "el Grammy en mejor canción del año y en ese momento acabaron nominados que Dricha sin minchakers por una canción que ni siquiera habían compuesto."

srcs.episode: Bitter Sweet Symphony: Quien fue su verdadero compositor?

podcast.title: Lyricist of "Bitter Sweet Symphony"
podcast.body: Richard Ashcroft is credited with writing the complete lyrics for The Verve's song "Bitter Sweet Symphony." This detail highlights his creative contribution to the track amidst the complex legal debates surrounding its musical composition. "la letra que es completamente escrita por Richard Ascro."

xref.title: Guitarist's Exit Before First Breakup (1998)
xref.body: On June 7, 1998, after a show in Rysho, Dusseldorf, Germany, singer Richard Ashcroft had a physical altercation with guitarist Nick McCabe, resulting in McCabe suffering a broken hand. McCabe subsequently decided to leave the band and was replaced by session guitarist B.J. Cole for the remaining tour commitments. "Which face took a pounding and Nick ended up with a broken hand. And with that, Nick decided he was done."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Eight-Year Separation and Reunion (2007)
xref.body: For eight years following their 1999 breakup, all members were adamant that a reunion would not happen. However, Nick McCabe began working with drummer Pete Salisbury, which prompted Richard Ashcroft to reconsider. Bass player Simon Jones was available, but guitarist Simon Tongue was deliberately excluded. The reunion was announced on June 26, 2007, after a period of eight years, one month, and 30 days apart. "For the next eight years, everyone was adamant that the verve would not reunite. The time tends to mellow people out."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Reunions: Some Lasted....and Sadly, Some Didn't ｜ Part 2

xref.title: Second Breakup Over Solo Career Ambitions (2008)
xref.body: The reunion was initially successful, especially regarding live performances, but it dissolved again around August 10, 2008. The breakup allegedly occurred because Nick McCabe and Simon Jones believed that Richard Ashcroft was using the reunion to re-establish his solo career, leading to a major conflict. "Why? Well, because Nick McCabe and Simon Jones allegedly believed that Richard Ashcroft was using this reunion just to get his solo career happening again."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Grammy Credit Discrepancy
xref.body: "Bittersweet Symphony" was nominated for a Grammy Award for Best Song, but the ballot controversially listed the songwriters as "Jagger Richards," reflecting the outcome of the publishing dispute rather than Richard Ashcroft's original composition. "And the ballot listed the songwriters of Bitter Sweet Symphony as Jagger Richards."
